cohort: The study included 3354 pregnant females, aged 18 years or older, with a BMI less than 35 kg/m², who initiated antenatal care before 14 weeks of gestation.
finding: Inadequate GWG (<25th centile) was associated with a higher odds of SGA, birth HC <10th centile, GDM, LBW, and birth length <10th centile, while excessive GWG (>75th centile) was associated with higher odds for emergency cesarean section and PIH.
mod_finding: Females with GWG >75th centile had higher odds for emergency cesarean section (OR: 1.7, 95% CI: 1.1, 2.7).
country: Brazil, Kenya, Pakistan, South Africa, Thailand, United Kingdom
birth_weight: N/A (LBW, SGA, LGA, macrosomia were outcomes, not inclusion criteria for birth weight)
gest_age: Antenatal care initiated before 14 weeks of gestation; weight measured from 14 to 40 weeks.
